objective: Remove exactly one rank from the accepted arbitrary-core bilinear shield while preserving physical coordinates and a single-use complete-tree payment.
prior_status: Arbitrary Boolean cores were covered only for full-column-rank M; positive-dimensional fibers were open. B01 separately covered one point defect at arbitrary positive codimension.
mathematical_delta: Proved that every rank-(m-1) bilinear shield with arbitrary Boolean core has a uniform 2^(2r)-atom squared spectrum and complete-tree retained-U loss at most 4 I_x and at most 2 I_total.
previous_bound: Arbitrary D only at nullity zero: accepted 4 I_x, with reviewer-derived 2 I_x pending fresh review.
new_bound: Arbitrary D at nullity one: 4 I_x and 2 I_total, uniformly over all physical kernel orientations.

constant_ledger.remaining_parameter: unbounded nullity with unequal conditional fiber spectra

verification.method: exact integer Walsh numerators plus independent direct truth-table reconstruction

remaining_obstacle: At nullity at least two, a Boolean core can have several unequal Fourier masses on each kernel coset. The resulting conditional fiber-spectrum entropy has no proved dimension-independent single-use payment in the original physical basis.
next_action: Derive the exact general-fiber entropy/upper-mass decomposition and test a payment of the average conditional fiber term by physical data-core influence plus retained terminal U, first at nullity two and then uniformly in nullity.
